verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is a refined petroleum distillate.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Most diesel fuel used in the United States is refined from crude oil (R2); Diesel fuel is refined from crude oil (R8); Diesel fuel is defined as a blend of petroleum-derived middle distillates (R12)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state diesel is refined from crude oil or petroleum distillates.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is denser than gasoline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel fuel is also more energy-dense than gasoline (R6); Diesel fuel is a heavier petroleum distillate than gasoline (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm diesel is heavier/more energy-dense, implying higher density.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is more energy-efficient than gasoline.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: diesel fuel offers a wide range of performance, efficiency (R2); Diesel fuel is more efficient than gasoline — in fact, it’s 20% more efficient (R3); Diesel engines are typically much more fuel-efficient (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute efficiency to diesel engines or broadly, not precisely to the fuel itself.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel powers compression-ignition engines in trucks, buses, trains, and farm equipment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel engines in trucks, trains, boats, and barges... public buses and school buses... farm and construction equipment (R2, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for uses in specified vehicles/equipment with compression-ignition implied.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel offers 11-40% better fuel economy than gasoline.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Diesel fuel is more efficient than gasoline — in fact, it’s 20% more efficient (R3); Diesels frequently get fuel mileage as much as 40 percent better (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Ranges mentioned but attributed to engines; 20-40% overlaps but not exact for fuel.

verifications.claim: Common types of diesel fuel include Diesel #2 (standard) and Diesel #1 (winter/cold weather).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel #1 (Grade 1-D)... best choice for situations like rough winter conditions (R3); Diesel #1... ideal for winter use... Diesel #2... most used (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly names #1 for winter/cold and #2 as standard/common.

verifications.claim: Diesel engines get up to 40% better mileage compared to similar gasoline vehicles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesels frequently get fuel mileage as much as 40 percent better than comparable weight vehicles with similarly sized gasoline engines
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for 40% better mileage in comparable vehicles.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel contains approx. 11% more usable energy per gallon than gasoline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel contains about 11% more energy per gallon than gasoline
verifications.reasoning: Precise match for 11% more energy per gallon.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel has lower volatility than gasoline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Regular gasoline is more volatile than diesel fuel (R6); low volatility of diesel fuel (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm lower volatility.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is less likely to ignite than gasoline if spilled.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: diesel fuel is less flammable and less explosive than other fuels (R2, R8); low volatility of diesel fuel that makes it less likely to ignite if spilled (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state less flammable/less likely to ignite when spilled.

verifications.claim: Diesel engines produce higher levels of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter (soot).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Pollution from diesel exhaust includes: Soot or particulate matter (PM); Oxides of nitrogen (NOx) (R5); gas engines emit lower levels of nitrogen oxides and particulate matter (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Directly lists NOx and PM/soot as diesel emissions; gas lower implies diesel higher.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel can gel or wax in extreme cold, clogging filters and hindering flow.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: one common challenge that can occur is gelling (R3); wax crystals form in the fuel, which can restrict flow... clog fuel filters (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Exact description of gelling/waxing in cold clogging filters.

verifications.claim: Diesel had approx. $3.52/gallon pump price vs $2.81/gallon for gasoline in Jan 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Regular Gasoline January 2026 Retail price: $2.81/gallon Diesel January 2026 Retail price: $3.52/gallon
verifications.reasoning: Exact prices and date match.

verifications.claim: Diesel #2 is Grade 2-D.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel #2 (Grade 2-D)
verifications.reasoning: Direct equivalence stated.

verifications.claim: Diesel #2 is the most common type of diesel fuel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The most common diesel fuel used today is Diesel #2 (R3); Diesel #2 is the most used diesel fuel (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly called most common.

verifications.claim: Diesel #2 is used for general transport and machinery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: use cases span multiple industries... construction equipment, commercial trucks, and buses
verifications.reasoning: Matches transport (trucks/buses) and machinery (construction).

verifications.claim: Diesel #2 can gel in cold weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Grade 2-D fuels don’t perform well in cold temperatures... one common challenge that can occur is gelling
verifications.reasoning: Directly states gelling issue for #2 in cold.

verifications.claim: Diesel #1 is Grade 1-D.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel #1 (Grade 1-D)
verifications.reasoning: Direct equivalence.

verifications.claim: Diesel #1 is lighter.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel #1 is a lighter, lower-viscosity fuel
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly called lighter.

verifications.claim: Diesel #1 has lower viscosity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel #1 also has lower viscosity than other diesel fuels (R3); lower-viscosity fuel (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement.

verifications.claim: Diesel #1 is resistant to cold temperatures.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: performs well in cold weather. Due to its higher cetane rating, Diesel #1 performs well in cold weather
verifications.reasoning: Described as best for cold weather.

verifications.claim: Biodiesel is produced from vegetable oils or animal fats.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: derived from materials such as animal fats, recycled grease, and vegetable oils (R3); made from vegetable oils or animal fats (R7, R9)
verifications.reasoning: Exact sources listed.

verifications.claim: Biodiesel is often blended with conventional diesel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Often blended with regular diesel to reduce emissions (R7); biodiesel is often blended with petroleum diesel (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as often blended.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is used in commercial trucks, buses, trains, and some cars.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel engines in trucks, trains... Diesel fuel is commonly used in public buses... Cars and light trucks (R2, R8)
verifications.reasoning: All listed uses directly supported.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is used in agricultural tractors, construction equipment, and cranes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: most farm and construction equipment (R2); agricultural machinery... construction equipment (R1); Construction – Heavy machinery such as cranes (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Farm/tractors, construction equipment explicit; cranes in construction.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is used in generators for standby power and in remote locations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: diesel engine generators to generate electricity... backup and emergency power supply. Most remote villages in Alaska use diesel generators (R2, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for generators, standby/emergency, remote.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel powers marine engines in ships and boats.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel engines in trucks, trains, boats, and barges (R2); marine diesel (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Boats/barges/ships directly listed.

verifications.claim: Diesel uses compression ignition.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: diesel engines... rely on compression ignition (R6, R10)
verifications.reasoning: Standard diesel characteristic confirmed.

verifications.claim: Diesel engines have no spark plugs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: diesels do not have spark plugs
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement.

verifications.claim: Gasoline uses spark ignition.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: gasoline engines rely on spark ignition (R6); spark plug ignites the fuel (R14)
verifications.reasoning: Standard gasoline characteristic confirmed.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is an oilier product compared to gasoline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: “It’s oily” (bingo!)
verifications.reasoning: Directly called oilier in context of myths.

verifications.claim: Diesel fuel is less refined compared to gasoline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Diesel is easier to refine; gas is more refined
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states gas more refined, diesel less.
